bilva
------------------------------------------
The बिल्व tree (Aegle marmelos), commonly called as the bel tree or the wood-apple tree, has long been considered as very sacred. Known as Śrīphala or Śrīvṛkṣa in the Sanskrit works, it is said to be dear to शिव, whose vegetal form it is supposed to be, to पार्वती or शक्ति and to Śrī or लक्ष्मी. Worship to this tree is an integral part of the elaborate दुर्गापूजा ritual.
Its leaves are invariably used in the worship of शिव and शक्ति. Amulets prepared out of these leaves are believed to be endowed with supernatural powers.
Medicines prepared out of the unripe fruit are credited with very effective powers of cure.
A pledge taken over the बिल्व leaf is considered too sacred to be broken.
‘Bilva’ is also the name of one of the mudrās or poses of hand and fingers, generally used in the worship of विष्णु.
